page: Amazon Web Services c6i.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base clock of 3.5 GHz. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 54 MB L3 cache. Memory resources total 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM operating at 3 GHz, delivering a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark evaluations place the processing capacity of the c6i.2xlarge firmly in the middle tier of standard cloud compute. Stress-ng scores show 1,892.79 for single-core and 7,730.15 for multi-core throughput, while Geekbench yields 1,581.0 and 6,011.0 respectively. General memory performance shows 58.16 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 41.69 GB/sec in write operations. Key CPU instruction sets include AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI, aiding vector calculations and cryptographic tasks. The instance demonstrates average execution in Clang compilation (8,044.0) and ray tracing (8,914.0).

Performance constraints appear primarily in memory-bound compression and large model machine learning execution. In multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, the system registers 30.72 GB/sec, falling into the bottom quartile of comparable instances. Large language model inference speeds reflect similar limitations; running a 7B parameter model yields 15.02 prompt processing tokens per second and 6.63 text generation tokens per second. Consequently, tasks demanding heavy local throughput or large neural network processing face hardware-level tradeoffs.

The 1:2 memory-to-core configuration makes the c6i.2xlarge cost-efficient for compute-bound processes that do not justify high memory overhead. With 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and 11.52 GB/sec static web serving throughput, the system fits distributed web servers, CI/CD compilation runners, batch computing, API gateways, and dedicated microservices that rely on predictable compute allocation.
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores. It features 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, delivering a tight 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a 54 MB L3 cache and support for AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance operates on the Nitro hypervisor, incorporates 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and does not provide local disk storage or hardware accelerators. Benchmark metrics place its single-core and multi-core execution in average performance tiers, highlighted by a Geekbench score of 6,011.0 and 7.92 million Redis set operations per second. However, heavy compression and larger LLM inference workloads demonstrate lower efficiency. The c6i.2xlarge is tailored for compute-driven tasks such as CI/CD build environments, batch processing jobs, API services, and high-throughput static web serving.
